scenes.heading: Observability Across Services
scenes.narration: Let's look at Observability Across Services, and how you debug one request as it travels through a fleet of Go microservices.

scenes.heading: The three pillars
items: Metrics: cheap aggregate numbers for alerting
Traces: one request's path across services
A shared trace ID ties all three together
scenes.narration: Observability rests on three pillars. Metrics are cheap aggregate time series like request rate and p99 latency, perfect for alerting. Logs are discrete high-cardinality events that give you detail. Traces stitch together the path of a single request across every service. Their real power comes from correlation: a shared trace ID lets you pivot from a metric spike to the exact trace to the exact log.

scenes.heading: How trace context propagates
steps: Every log line is stamped with it
scenes.narration: Here's how a trace stays connected. At the edge, a trace ID is generated and stored in the request's context. When a service calls downstream, an instrumented transport like otelhttp serializes that context into a W3C traceparent header. The receiving service extracts it and continues the same trace instead of starting a new one. Meanwhile, your logger reads the same context and stamps the trace ID onto every line.

scenes.heading: Creating a child span
scenes.narration: This is what instrumentation looks like in practice. tracer.Start reads the incoming context and creates a child span named fetchOrder, attaching the order ID as an attribute. The deferred span.End records its duration when the function returns, so the database call shows up as a segment in the trace waterfall. On failure we call RecordError and SetStatus, which marks the span red in the backend so the slow or failing hop is instantly visible.

scenes.text: Correlated telemetry turns 'which of twelve services is slow?' into a single trace lookup.
scenes.narration: The payoff is huge. When every metric, trace, and log shares one trace ID, an incident stops being hours of tailing logs on each box. You jump from a latency alert to the slow trace to the exact logs for that request, collapsing mean time to resolution across the whole fleet.
